title: Ambient proper/open identity word for an integral refinement
statement: For a coefficient sheaf R, an identity compactification refinement, and an open comparison whose transpose is the open adjunction unit, the corresponding geometric proper/open word is the identity on every ambient derived object.

source.place: the identity clause, ambient proper/open word after the open-adjunction transpose

proof.text: The coefficient compatibility hg for identity followed by c.g forces R.pull(identity) to equal the canonical ring inverse-image identity: cancel the invertible inverse-image compositor and inverse image of R.pull(c.g), then use naturality and the identity law for the site compositor.

Construct module direct image along identity by pushforwardCongr₂ for the site pullbackId and the resulting coefficient identity. Its section maps are restriction along pullbackId.inv. The section normalization of modulePushComposition_existsUnique and the two pullbackComp identity laws prove both module direct-image compositor unit laws. Conjugating gives the corresponding module inverse-image laws.

Exact localization preserves the two module inverse-image unit laws. For one orientation apply the existing generic derive_right_unit theorem. For the other use the same localization calculation with an explicit transport isomorphism, applying mapDerivedCategoryNatIso to the module identity and its whiskering, and then the derived-composition unitor law. These identify the specified geometric inverse-image compositors with the derived identity comparison.

Use restriction_identity_component to identify the identity refinement restriction with pullback of the conjugate identity direct-image comparison. The hypothesis hε, injectivity of the open adjunction Hom-equivalence, and inverse cancellation identify that comparison with ε.inv. The identity_comparison and conjugate_paste_identity calculations, proved privately for arbitrary category universes, identify the geometric proper compositor with its proper pushforward. The final word is therefore an isomorphism inverse followed by its hom.

theorem integral_normalized_ring_refinement_identity_core
    (R : PurCompactSupport.Coefficients.{max u v})
    {X Y : Scheme.{max u v}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {c : Compactification f}
    (hi : R.pull (c.i ≫ (Compactification.Refinement.id c).hom) =
      proEtaleRingCompositeCoefficients c.i (Compactification.Refinement.id c).hom
        (R.ring c.Z) (R.ring c.Z) (R.ring X)
        (R.pull (Compactification.Refinement.id c).hom) (R.pull c.i))
    (hg : R.pull ((Compactification.Refinement.id c).hom ≫ c.g) =
      proEtaleRingCompositeCoefficients (Compactification.Refinement.id c).hom c.g
        (R.ring Y) (R.ring c.Z) (R.ring c.Z)
        (R.pull c.g) (R.pull (Compactification.Refinement.id c).hom))
    (K : DerivedCategory (pbcModules X (R.ring X)))
    (ε : (PurCompactSupport.openExtension R c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj K ≅
      (PurCompactSupport.push R (Compactification.Refinement.id c).hom).obj
        ((PurCompactSupport.openExtension R c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))
    (hε : (PurCompactSupport.openDerivedAdjunction R c.i).homEquiv _ _ ε.hom ≫
      PurCompactSupport.refinementRestriction R (Compactification.Refinement.id c) hi K =
        (PurCompactSupport.openDerivedAdjunction R c.i).unit.app K) :
    ((PurCompactSupport.geometricPushComposition R
        (Compactification.Refinement.id c).hom c.g hg ≪≫
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun h ↦ PurCompactSupport.push R h)
        (Compactification.Refinement.id c).hom_g)).symm.app
        ((PurCompactSupport.openExtension R c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)).hom ≫
      (PurCompactSupport.push R c.g).map ε.inv = 𝟙 _
